fix_note: Saving a board no longer sends its update ping to every connected user — the ping now goes only to the board owner's session, the way the board's own live-editing events already travel room-by-room (per-user notification scoping, as in Slack/Notion). Private boards stay private in the realtime layer too.

Choosing Private (or Followers) in the post composer now actually sets the post's audience — before, every post was stored public no matter what was picked, even though the feed already enforced private/followers visibility on read (Facebook-style audience selector: the choice is honored, and the post itself shows its audience). The composer also resets to Public after each post, so a one-off private post no longer leaves the selector stuck on Private, and your own non-public posts carry a Private/Followers badge in the Social home feed.

Events now record a visibility when created (Private by default, Public on request — the Google Calendar / Eventbrite create-time choice), the planner offers the control in the create form and on the event itself, event lists show Private/Public and whether the public page is live, and publishing a public page for a private event is refused with a plain explanation instead of silently going public. Verified end to end on the real domain code: default private, publish refused while private, unpublish always allowed, publish succeeds after flipping to Public, junk values fall back to private.

A council member can now prepare a proposal privately: drafts are visible to their author alone — other members' proposal lists no longer include them, a draft can't be found or voted on by anyone else, and the shared audit trail records the creation without the draft's title. Moving the proposal out of Draft (to Discussion) shares it with the council exactly as before, and the chamber already labels the author's own drafts as Draft. Verified on the real domain code with two members: draft hidden from the second member end to end, then visible and votable after the author published it.

The Household lens badge no longer says 'Real but static / open-access dataset' over a family's own records. That wording described only the lens's reference content; the badge caption now names both halves — reference content (seasonal checklists, maintenance schedules) is real and from open sources, and the household's own records (members, meal plans, chores, budgets) are the member's alone, saved privately on their account. Done as a household entry in the shared depth-badge override table, the same mechanism other lenses use when the generic caption misdescribes them.

Segments, clubs and challenges are shared platform-wide by design (Strava parity — public leaderboards and clubs), while activities, goals, PRs and gear are per-user. Two things hid that: the domain's parity comments claimed everything was per-user scoped, and the create flows never said the thing being made is public. The comments now state the real split, and the segment, club and challenge create forms each carry a plain note — 'Shared with everyone on Concord' — before the create button, matching how Strava presents its public segments and clubs.

Reminders could only ever be aimed at a real outbound destination — the channel was coerced to SMS or email, so there was no way to keep a reminder as a private note. A third channel, 'none', is now accepted: the form offers it as 'Just for me — don't send', the target field is replaced with a plain 'Stays in your list only — nothing is sent' note, the reminder is stored with channel none, lists with a 'just me' badge and a 'not sent' marker instead of a red no-contact warning, and dispatch skips it entirely — it is never queued for the operator to send and never failed for having no target. Verified on the real domain module: a private reminder stays 'scheduled' through a dispatch that queues a normal SMS reminder.

The /dtu/<id> page dressed everyone — including the signed-in owner of a private DTU — in signed-out chrome: a Sign in / Join Concord header, a bare tier badge with no Private label, and Fork as the only action, with no owner controls and no delete. Access control itself was sound (the server refuses anonymous reads of private DTUs and the record is absent from search); the view simply never asked who was looking. It now reads the session: a signed-in viewer gets a 'Signed in as …' header instead of join prompts, a non-public DTU (visibility private, or scope local/private) carries a Private badge beside the tier badge, the Fork CTA links straight to the fork target when signed in, and the owner gets an owner strip — 'This is your DTU' — with a two-step delete against the standing DELETE /api/dtus/:id route (the server still enforces delete ownership), ending on a plain deleted state with the server's error shown if the delete fails.

Poems are private to the account and sharing is an explicit opt-in (workshop-share snapshots a poem into the shared workshop), but nothing labelled the state — lists and the editor showed only the writing status (draft/revising/finished), so a member could not tell a private poem from one already shared with every workshop reader. poem-list and poem-detail now carry sharedToWorkshop, computed for the caller from the workshop store, and the collection list, the workspace list and the editor all render the audience in plain words beside the status: 'Private' (or 'Private — only you' in the editor) versus 'Shared to workshop'. Verified on the real domain module: both poems read false before sharing, the shared one flips to true in list and detail, the kept one stays false, and unsharing flips it back.

Rolls carried no visibility at all — no field on the record and no label on the page — so a member could neither tell nor state a roll's audience. Rolls now record a visibility: validated public/private at create, private by default (junk values fall back to private, never wider), changeable through shoot-update, and carried by shoot-list and the hydrated durable shapes — rolls that predate the field read as private, which is their true state, since nothing in the lens reads another member's rolls today; the field states the audience honestly instead of leaving it to guesswork, and a future public surface will gate on a real recorded value. The roll header on the photography page carries the labelled Visibility control (Private/Public) wired to shoot-update. Verified on the real domain module: default private, junk falls back, explicit public stored, update flips and junk update falls back.

'Publish Project' was the only submit and it published silently: the server has always honoured a published flag (create stores it, update flips it, projectList hides drafts from non-owners, projectView refuses them, the feed only carries published work) but the form never sent it, never labelled a published project, and confirmed nothing. The form now offers a Visibility choice — 'Published — everyone can see it' or 'Draft — only you' — sends it on create and update, restores it when editing, and names the submit for the choice ('Publish Project' / 'Save as Draft'); every project card shows Published or 'Draft — only you'; and a successful save raises a toast stating the audience ('Project published — everyone can see it.' / 'Draft saved — only you can see it.'). Verified on the real domain module: a draft is stored unpublished, a stranger's direct view of it is refused as not found, and flipping it to published opens it. Frontend-only change; the pin's server-contract assertions pass on the base by design — they pin the contract the form now uses.
